name: Badlands National Park
unique: Striped eroding buttes, bighorn sheep and the largest protected mixed-grass prairie in the country, with a loop road that puts you inside the formations.
buzz: Sunrise and sunset turn the rock orange; midday is flat. Watch for bison on the road and rattlesnakes on trails.

name: Custer State Park
company: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks
unique: A 1,300-head bison herd, begging burros, granite spires and the Needles Highway, a road that threads through rock tunnels barely wider than a car.
buzz: The wildlife loop is the highlight; the Needles Highway is genuinely thrilling. Bison jams can last an hour.

name: Mount Rushmore
unique: Four sixty-foot faces blasted into granite over fourteen years, with a night lighting ceremony and a sculptor's studio that shows how it was done.
buzz: People are surprised how moved they are; the evening lighting is the best time. Parking is the only cost.

name: National Music Museum
unique: One of the great instrument collections in the world, with Stradivarius violins, early keyboards and a saxophone once owned by Adolphe Sax.
buzz: Musicians call it a pilgrimage and the collection is bigger than the town; the staff will demonstrate some instruments.

name: The Mammoth Site
unique: A sinkhole where 60 mammoths fell in and died 26,000 years ago, now an active dig inside a building over the bone bed.
buzz: The bone bed is the real thing and the paleontologists work in front of you in summer; children can join a dig with a reservation.

name: Wind Cave
unique: One of the longest caves in the world and the first national park for a cave, famous for boxwork, thin calcite fins that look like honeycomb.
buzz: The natural entrance tour is the classic; rangers explain the barometric wind that breathes in and out of the cave. Book ahead.

name: Needles Highway
unique: A 14 mile road through granite spires and two tunnels blasted through the rock, including a one lane eye of the needle passage.
buzz: The tunnels and the Cathedral Spires are the photographs and the road is narrow; drive it early to avoid the tour buses.

name: Spearfish Canyon
unique: A 22 mile limestone canyon with three waterfalls, a scenic byway and trails to Bridal Veil Falls, 15 minutes from Spearfish.
buzz: The drive is the attraction and the falls are short walks; it is the setting for Dances with Wolves and the canyon is busy in fall.

name: Sturgis Motorcycle Rally
unique: Half a million motorcycles take over a town of 7,000 for a week, with concerts, a mile of vendors and the Black Hills as the ride.
buzz: It is loud, hot and utterly singular; nonriders love the spectacle. Book lodging a year ahead or camp.

name: 1880 Train
unique: A steam train that climbs a 4 percent grade through the Black Hills between Hill City and Keystone, with open cars and a view of the granite peaks.
buzz: The steam engine and the climb are the reason to ride and the open car is the seat to book; the round trip takes two hours.

name: Bear Butte State Park
company: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks
unique: A sacred butte where Lakota and Cheyenne people still come for vision quests, with a trail to the summit and prayer offerings along the way.
buzz: The climb is steep and the site is sacred, so visitors are asked to stay on the trail and respect the offerings; the view reaches the Black Hills.

name: Black Hills Institute
unique: The fossil laboratory and museum behind the commercial diggers, with a T. rex named Sue's original bones and a wall of ammonites.
buzz: The prep lab is the reason paleontology people stop and the museum is small; the institute also runs digs you can join.

name: Crazy Horse Memorial
unique: A mountain being carved into a 563-foot horseman since 1948, with a Native American museum, a sculptor's home and a laser show at night.
buzz: The scale is staggering and the progress is slow; the museum is excellent and the controversy is worth understanding.

name: Laura Ingalls Wilder Homestead
unique: The surveyor's house and the Ingalls family homes from the Little House books, with a pageant in summer and the prairie around them unchanged.
buzz: Readers come from other countries and the guides know the books and the family; the summer pageant is the local tradition.

name: Deadwood
unique: A gold-rush gulch town where Wild Bill Hickok was shot, with the actual-saloon rebuilds, a cemetery on the hill and legal casino poker in every other storefront.
buzz: The history is well presented and the town is fun; the casino carpet is part of the charm. Catch the trial reenactment.

name: Akta Lakota Museum
unique: A museum on the Missouri with a collection of Lakota beadwork, quillwork and star quilts, free and run by the school.
buzz: The star quilts and beadwork are the highlights and it is free; the river overlook outside is the photograph.

name: Falls Park
unique: The falls that gave the city its name, where the Big Sioux drops over pink quartzite ledges in a downtown park with a viewing tower and the remains of a mill.
buzz: The falls and the tower are the photograph and the park is free; the lights at night in summer are the local tradition.

name: Redlin Art Center
unique: A gallery built to hold 160 Terry Redlin paintings of small town and wildlife America, given free to the public by the artist.
buzz: The scale of the gift and the building are the surprise; it is free and the paintings are more nostalgic than kitsch.

name: South Dakota Cultural Heritage Center
unique: The state history museum with a strong Native American collection, a sod house and the story of the Black Hills gold rush, on the capitol grounds.
buzz: The Native galleries and the sod house are the reasons to stop; it is a good rainy day and the capital building next door is free.

name: Lewis and Clark Lake
unique: A reservoir on the Missouri below Gavins Point Dam with 90 miles of shoreline, sandy beaches and some of the best walleye fishing in the state.
buzz: The lake is the summer water for the region and the dam is the history; the wind makes afternoon boating rough.

name: Prehistoric Indian Village
unique: A thousand year old village of earth lodges under a protective dome, with an active dig and a lab where students process what they find.
buzz: The dig under the dome is the reason to come and the site is active in summer; it pairs with the Corn Palace down the road.

name: South Dakota State Fair
unique: The state fair on the prairie with livestock shows, a draft horse pull, a carnival and grandstand concerts.
buzz: The livestock barns and the horse pull are the real fair and the concerts draw the region; it is hot and the parking is in fields.

name: Adams Museum
unique: A museum in a 1892 brick building with Wild Bill Hickok's guns, a two headed calf and the nugget that started the gold rush.
buzz: The collection is odd and local and the building is the setting; it is cheap and pairs with the town walk.

name: Evans Plunge
unique: A naturally warm mineral spring pool with a water slide, the oldest attraction in the Black Hills, in a sandstone building over the spring.
buzz: The water is 87 degrees and the slide is a surprise in a historic bathhouse; it is a good family stop after the Mammoth Site.

name: Gavins Point Dam
unique: A Missouri River dam with a visitor center, a fish hatchery and a below dam tailwater where bald eagles winter by the dozen.
buzz: The eagles in winter are the reason photographers come and the dam tour explains the flood control; the visitor center is free.

name: Hill City
unique: A small Black Hills town on the Mickelson Trail with a main street of galleries, a winery and the 1880 Train depot, surrounded by granite peaks.
buzz: The town is the base for the Mickelson Trail and the train; it is quieter than Keystone and the food is better.

name: McCrory Gardens
unique: Twenty five acres of display gardens and a prairie restoration on the university campus, with a children's garden and a rose garden.
buzz: The prairie and the trial gardens are the reason gardeners come and it is free; peak bloom is July.

name: Reptile Gardens
unique: A 1937 reptile park with the largest collection in the world, alligator and snake shows, and a prairie dog town you can walk through.
buzz: Children love the shows and adults are surprised by the botanical gardens; the park is old fashioned and well run.

name: Sioux Falls SculptureWalk
unique: A rotating outdoor gallery of 60 sculptures along the downtown streets, each for sale, with a map that turns the city into a gallery.
buzz: The walk is free and the pieces change every year; locals vote on a favorite and the winner is bought for the city.

name: South Dakota Art Museum
unique: A university museum with the Harvey Dunn prairie paintings and a Marghab linen collection, free on the South Dakota State campus.
buzz: The Dunn paintings are the reason art people stop and the linens are the surprise; it is free and takes an hour.

name: South Dakota State Capitol
unique: A Neoclassical capitol with a copper dome and a rotunda of native stone, in a town of 14,000 on the Missouri.
buzz: The rotunda and the governor's reception room are the quick tour and it is free; the view from the capitol steps is the prairie.

name: Washington Pavilion
unique: A 1890s school building turned arts and science center, with a visual arts museum, a discovery center and a domed theater.
buzz: The science center is the family draw and the art galleries are quiet; the building itself is the landmark on the downtown skyline.

name: Wall Drug
unique: A drugstore that became a 76,000-square-foot roadside empire on the strength of free ice water and a hundred miles of billboards, with a giant jackalope and a chapel.
buzz: It is a tourist trap that knows it and leans in; the donuts and the free water are the tradition. A perfect Badlands pit stop.

name: Bramble Park Zoo
unique: A small zoo in a city park with a carousel and a train, plus a collection of big cats and primates, in a town of 22,000.
buzz: Parents like the size and the train and the zoo is cheap; the park around it has a swimming pool and picnic areas.

name: Corn Palace
unique: A 1921 Moorish-style palace whose facade is re-covered every year in murals made of eleven colors of corn and grain.
buzz: It is free, fast and better than the jokes suggest; the interior is a basketball arena. Worth the I-90 stop.

name: Dacotah Prairie Museum
unique: A county museum in a 1911 bank building with a prairie town street, a one room school and the story of the Dakota conflict.
buzz: The street scene and the school are good with children and the collection is local and specific; it is free will donation.

name: Lake Herman State Park
company: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks
unique: A wooded lake park with a campground, a beach and a historic stone cabin, in the lake country of eastern South Dakota.
buzz: The lake is quiet and the campground is shaded; it is a good stop between Sioux Falls and the Minnesota line.

name: Storybook Land
unique: A free storybook park with nursery rhyme buildings, a small train and a yellow brick road, in a town that takes its L. Frank Baum connection seriously.
buzz: Parents say it is the right size for children under eight and the train is the hit; the rides cost a few dollars.

name: Cosmos Mystery Area
unique: A shack in the Black Hills where balls roll uphill and people seem to lean at impossible angles, a classic gravity illusion attraction that never explains itself.
buzz: It is a roadside gag and the guides lean into the fun; kids are delighted. Twenty minutes from Mount Rushmore.
